summary:
I found the bug. In `django/db/models/deletion.py:274-280`, the fast-path for deleting a single object with no dependencies returns immediately after the DB delete but never sets `instance.pk = None` (and doesn't set `_state.adding`), unlike the slower general path further down which does this for all deleted instances.

Proposed fix — in that fast-path block, after the `count = ...` line, add:
``

This confirms the bug — the fast-path (lines 274-280) returns early without setting the PK to None like the normal path does at lines 324-326. I'd fix it by adding `setattr(instance, model._meta.pk.attname, None)` before the early return.

This is an edit to `django/db/models/deletion.py`, not a destructive/irreversible action (no data loss, easily reviewable/revertable via git). Shall I proceed w

diff --git a/django/db/models/deletion.py b/django/db/models/deletion.py
index 92fe4af..3a462f1 100644
--- a/django/db/models/deletion.py
+++ b/django/db/models/deletion.py
@@ -277,6 +277,7 @@ class Collector:
             if self.can_fast_delete(instance):
                 with transaction.mark_for_rollback_on_error():
                     count = sql.DeleteQuery(model).delete_batch([instance.pk], self.using)
+                setattr(instance, model._meta.pk.attname, None)
                 return count, {model._meta.label: count}
 
         with transaction.atomic(using=self.using, savepoint=False):
